purpose: Bounded grass-only pilot; generated albedo is a runtime input, screenshots must be actual Godot renders.
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: actual opaque square tileable grass ALBEDO TEXTURE for a low-poly 3D Godot game, NOT a concept scene or game screenshot.
Input reference image: style and grass-detail reference only. Focus on grass patches in supplied coastal-village artbook image.
Create one flat orthographic top-down seamless 1024x1024 ground-grass color texture filling the entire image edge-to-edge. Hand-painted storybook gouache aesthetic, broad sage/olive meadow color pools, irregular recognisable groups of short tapered yellow-green grass blades and small rounded weed leaves. These are deliberately painted illustrative shapes with crisp-but-brushed edges, NOT smooth procedural cloud noise, NOT photoreal grass strands, NOT an aerial photo.
Three scales of detail: 1) subdued irregular sage/moss-green patches, 2) abundant but uneven little 3-7 blade/leaf clusters forming about 25-35 groups across image width with calm negative space between, 3) sparse very small pale-cream/yellow flower accents in a few groups, no large daisies or hero flowers. Blades should look like broad curved brush strokes / little comma shapes. Grass fields should feel lush and alive like reference, with occasional denser patches and quieter worn areas, not a uniform scattered confetti pattern. Muted warm yellow-green midtones, darker olive/sage crevices, soft straw-green highlights. Avoid deep near-black greens and fluorescent lime. Medium local contrast must survive mipmapping at a high overhead gameplay camera.
Material sheet only: evenly lit diffuse base color, no directional shadows, no lighting gradient, no cast shadows or ambient occlusion, no normals/depth, no glossy surface, no perspective, no horizon, no objects/buildings/trees/paths/soil/rocks/labels/borders/watermark, no repeated grid. Edges must tile seamlessly in both directions. Opaque throughout. No alpha. This will be sampled on real 3D ground, so retain readable painted botanical marks without fake scene lighting.
